messages:
priya: FYI seeing a spike in OIDC introspection failures starting ~09:12 UTC, a bunch of auth flows are falling back or failing.  
priya: sample error in logs: 
```
oauth: introspect: jwks fetch failed status=403 url=https://idp.example.com/.well-known/jwks.json
verify: token could not be validated
```
priya: we moved the JWKS behind CloudFront yesterday for rate limiting. could be the cause. @diego any ideas? :thinking_face:
evan: hmm 403 on jwks fetch usually means either origin blocked the CF request or our introspector IPs blocked. Does CF use a new Host or auth header?
diego: CloudFront adds a header and can sign requests if origin is private. If origin has an allowlist for our introspect service IPs that could be the culprit. Also CF might cache a 403 for the JWKS which is bad.
katie: ok, while you debug, SCIM provisioning is reporting "invalid signature" for some service-accounts and we're seeing RBAC deltas applied then reverted. I think the provisioning webhook is failing auth checks and our repair job is toggling roles.
priya: exact symptom: user provisioning job tries to PATCH /users/:id -> 401 from the identity service because token verification fails, then a scheduled reconciliation step re-applies an older role. audit shows deprovision then re-add.
priya: pasted curl result from our introspector host: 
```
curl -i -H "Host: idp.example.com" https://idp-edge.example-cdn.net/.well-known/jwks.json
HTTP/2 403\ncontent-type: application/json\ncache-control: max-age=86400\n{ "error": "forbidden" }
```
priya: notice CF returning cache-control 86400 for a 403 which means the error will stick.
diego: that's the killer. If CF caches 403 for a long TTL, all our services will keep failing until the TTL expires. Change: set error caching to 0 for the JWKS path and allow the introspection user-agent through origin-level allowlist.
ev an: (typo) evan: to add: our introspector rotates a local JWKS cache every 5m as a fallback. But if CF returned 403 and cache-control made it 24h, the fallback isn't triggered. We should update fallback policy to ignore origin cache-control on error responses. Also short-term we can seed the runtime with the current public keys to stop the churn.
katie: seeding keys would fix verification for a bit, but SCIM service uses client credentials stored in DB encrypted with KMS. Could the KMS rotation also be playing into this? I see a KMS Rekey event 09:10 UTC in audit.
diego: KMS rekey is unrelated to JWKS fetch. KMS affects stored client secrets decryption; if that failed we'd see decrypt errors not jwks fetch 403. Check logs for "kms.Decrypt failed".
priya: checked: no kms.Decrypt errors around 09:12. so separate. good.
idp-bot: Automated alert: JWKS origin returned 403 for CloudFront request id=CF12345 path=/.well-known/jwks.json at 2025-12-06T09:12:03Z
priya: plan: 1) ask infra to set CloudFront error caching for jwks path to 0 and allow our introspect service role/IP (change request filed: INF-827). 2) push a small rollout to seed current public keys to runtimes (evan to handle). 3) temp increase reconciliation cooldown for SCIM to avoid flip-flop audit noise (katie to coordinate). 4) add a postmortem checklist entry for JWKS behind CDN.
ev an: ETA on seeding keys: 15min, will push a single-version config to all regions.
diego: infra note: also ensure origin responds with Cache-Control: public, max-age=60 for jwks success responses and set custom error responses to not cache 403/5xx. Without that CF will keep serving stale errors.
katie: I'll hold the SCIM reconciliation jobs and annotate the audit events so CS doesn't get noisy alerts. Also saving the audit IDs to tie to root cause.
priya: one more: add an audit rule to flag when JWKS fetches start returning 4xx from edge. Should have alerted earlier. filing SEC-459.
evan: rolling seed out now -> 10.0% region eu-west then cascade. watching metrics.
idp-bot: Notice: 10% rollout completed, jwks seeded to runtimes in eu-west.
priya: great. keep me posted. once origin ACLs and CF error TTL change land we can unpause SCIM reconciliation.
diego: possible followup: consider serving JWKS from a static S3 origin with signed URLs scoped to the CDN, and put strict monitoring on jwks fetch latency and 4xx rates.
priya: thanks all. postmortem notes will include timeline + remediation + necessary alert rules. :white_check_mark:
